name: What if a commercial project runs over budget?

mainEntity.name: What should happen if a commercial project starts going over budget?
mainEntity.text: What should happen if a commercial project starts going over budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: When a project starts to exceed budget, the response should be immediate and structured. The manager should isolate whether the issue comes from scope growth, bidding gaps, labor pricing, schedule delay, or unforeseen site conditions. Then the budget forecast should be updated so the owner can see the real exposure, not just the original estimate. If necessary, the team can re-sequence work, adjust finishes, defer nonessential items, or use contingency strategically. Communication is critical because waiting until the end usually makes the problem worse. A good commercial project manager does not hide overruns; they identify them early and present clear options. Owners should also ask for a formal approval process for any cost increase so there are no surprises later.
acceptedAnswer.description: If a project goes over budget, the manager should identify the cause, update the forecast, prioritize critical items, and present options to reduce cost or re-scope work. The earlier the issue is addressed, the easier it is to protect the final outcome.
